result.summary:
Ran docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md against the REQ-036 diff (commit 188038e, reviewed at 263d7c4) by reading the actual shipped code, not the design doc's or BACKEND-DEV's claims about it.

S9 (idempotency/restart-safety, AC4) -- traced by hand, kill-mid-batch simulation: apps/bot/src/scheduler/autoDeclineJobs.ts's makeAutoDeclineJob loop calls autoDeclineRequest(db, registrationId, evaluationTime) per candidate (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts:1960-2006), which runs inside ONE db.transaction: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, decideRejectionOutcome (pure, reused unchanged from REQ-035), and on 'reject' a single UPDATE registrations SET admission='rejected' plus one writeAuditLog call in the SAME transaction. Mechanism 2 (state guard): decideRejectionOutcome returns 'not-requested' for any row whose admission is no longer 'requested' -- so a row already flipped to 'rejected' by a prior tick (or by an organizer) is structurally excluded from selectRegistrationsForAutoDecline's own `WHERE admission = 'requested'` clause on the next tick; no second UPDATE, no second audit row is reachable even in principle, since the selection query itself cannot re-surface it. Mechanism 1 (send guard): sendLedgeredNotification's step 4 (apps/bot/src/domain/notification.ts:135-145) is a single INSERT into notification_ledger guarded by uq_notification_ledger_registration_kind (UNIQUE(registration_id, kind), confirmed at apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts line ~424); a second call for the same (registrationId, 'registration_auto_declined') pair hits the Postgres unique-violation path (code 23505) and returns skipped-already-sent with no second send. Verified these are genuinely independent per design §0.3/§3.4 and by reading the code: Mechanism 2 lives entirely in registrations.admission + the selection WHERE clause and has zero reference to notification_ledger; Mechanism 1 lives entirely in the ledger's unique index and has zero reference to registrations.admission -- a bug disabling one (e.g. a hypothetical missing WHERE clause) would not be silently masked by the other, since the auto-decline job's own step 3 (apps/bot/src/scheduler/autoDeclineJobs.ts:116) skips the notification call entirely when outcome.kind !== 'reject', meaning a Mechanism-2 failure that let an already-rejected row through would still attempt a real UPDATE+audit (visible, not masked) before Mechanism 1 is even consulted. Kill-mid-batch trace (3 candidates, kill after candidate 1 commits, before candidate 2 starts): on restart, runner.ts's immediate first tick re-runs selection; candidate 1 (admission already 'rejected') is excluded by Mechanism 2, never re-selected, autoDeclineRequest never called again for it (Mechanism 1 not even reached); candidates 2 and 3 (untouched, still 'requested', no ledger row) are re-selected and each transitions/sends exactly once. Total: 3 transitions, 3 sends across both runs -- matches AC4's required count. No further transitions on any later tick since all three rows are then 'rejected'.

S10 (transactional, blocked-user-skip) -- confirmed both apps/bot/src/scheduler/urgencyJobs.ts and apps/bot/src/scheduler/autoDeclineJobs.ts call sendLedgeredNotification with classification: 'transactional' as a literal (not a variable, not defaulted -- SendClassification has no optional/default per notification.ts's own AC5 comment), so step 3's broadcast_opt_in gate (notification.ts:128) is structurally unreached for both new kinds, and step 2's unconditional blocked check (notification.ts:122-124) applies to both exactly as it does to every other existing kind. Neither new call site bypasses sendLedgeredNotification -- both jobs call it directly with no alternate send path.

S8 (audit) -- autoDeclineRequest (registration.ts:1995-2002) writes exactly one writeAuditLog row per successful transition, actorUserId: null (system-initiated, matches the schema's own nullable actor_user_id and its existing comment), inside the same db.transaction as the admission UPDATE (both inside the single `return db.transaction(async (tx) => {...})` body, both using `tx`). The 'not-found'/'not-requested' branches return before any UPDATE or writeAuditLog call -- zero audit rows for a no-op, matching AC2/AC6's 'approved/rejected rows untouched' requirement.

registration_closes_at IS NULL -> ends_at fallback ordering -- re-verified against the shipped selectRegistrationsForAutoDecline (autoDeclineJobs.ts:40-77) and selectRegistrationsForUrgencyNotice (urgencyJobs.ts:44-69) independently, not by trusting the design doc's proof: the urgency job's selection has no reference to registrationClosesAt at all -- it fires purely off events.startsAt, 48h before start, regardless of when (or whether) registration closes. The auto-decline job's selection only fires at MAX(effective close instant) where effective close = registrationClosesAt if not null else endsAt -- and endsAt is always >= startsAt (validateAgenda/createEvent's own ends-after-starts invariant, domain/event.ts:182-186), so the auto-decline trigger instant can never precede startsAt, and therefore can never precede startsAt - 48h (the urgency trigger instant). This holds even in the NULL-registrationClosesAt/ends_at-fallback case: the auto-decline instant is endsAt (>= startsAt) which is always >= startsAt - 48h. No window exists where auto-decline could fire before the urgency window has had a chance to surface the request; independently confirmed, not re-quoted from CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR.

Single-organizer urgency recipient -- getPrimaryOrganizerIdForChapter (registration.ts:1933-1944) queries `WHERE role='organizer' AND chapter_id = $1 ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT 1`, called with candidate.chapterId which is selected directly from `events.chapterId` in the SAME join selectRegistrationsForUrgencyNotice performs (urgencyJobs.ts:51-58) -- the chapterId passed in is always the actual chapter of the event the pending request belongs to, read fresh from the events table at selection time, never a cached/stale value. The query itself filters strictly on role='organizer' scoped to that exact chapterId, so the recipient is always a currently-assigned organizer of that event's own chapter -- no cross-chapter leak, no stale-user path. A chapter with zero organizers returns null and the push is skipped (no ledger row, no error) -- an availability gap, not an authorization gap, and independently covered by the always-fresh list marker (organizerRequests.ts).

S11 (no PII in logs) -- writeAuditLog payload for registration.auto_decline is `{ eventId }` only (registration.ts:2001) -- no phone/email/name. composeAutoDeclineNotice (autoDeclineJobs.ts:82-97) and composeUrgencyNotice (urgencyJobs.ts:73-91) interpolate only the event title into catalog strings -- no user PII appears in either composed message or in the audit payload.

Schema/migration -- confirmed zero migration files in the diff (git diff --name-only 188038e~1..263d7c4 lists only apps/bot/src/** and docs/handoffs/issues files, no drizzle/ files); every column referenced (registrations.admission, events.startsAt/endsAt/registrationClosesAt, audit_log.actor_user_id, notification_ledger's existing unique index) pre-exists unchanged. No S13 migration sign-off applicable -- N/A, no column/table drop/rename/rewrite in this diff.

AC8 catalog check -- grepped both new scheduler files for inline literal user-facing strings: none found: both composeXNotice functions source all text via getCatalog(lang).organizerRequests.* / catalog.autoDecline.notification. en.ts/ru.ts both carry parallel urgentMarker/urgentNotification/autoDecline.notification keys; apps/bot/src/i18n/catalogs.test.ts's existing runtime parity check (types.ts's Catalog type + `satisfies Catalog` on both locale files) structurally enforces key-set parity. BACKEND-DEV's step-02 handoff explicitly records the wording as provisional pending the product owner, satisfying this requirement's own explicit instruction.

All applicable invariants (S8, S9, S10, S11) verified independently against the shipped code with constructed negative cases, not the producer's or CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's self-report. S1-S7, S12, S13, S14 are N/A to this diff -- it touches no consent flow, no role/EventStaff authorization surface, no qr_token/InviteCode, no check-in, no capacity, no export, no deletion/anonymization, no speaker publication.
